steps.title: Sauté a fish fillet
steps.prompt: Put the stages of sautéing a fish fillet to order in order, from the pan to the plate. One stage does not belong.
steps: Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat
Add a thin film of oil or clarified butter and wait until it shimmers
As the fat shimmers, season the dried fillet and dredge it in flour, shaking off every loose speck
Lay it in presentation side down, away from you, and press it flat for a moment
Leave it alone until the crust forms and it lets go of the pan
Turn it once, lower the heat and finish it gently
Lift it out and plate it presentation side up
steps.distractor: Crowd every fillet on the ticket into the pan at once so the order goes out together
steps.why: The pan is hot before the fat and the fat before the fish, which is dredged at the last moment so the coat stays dry. Left alone, it releases once the crust forms; crowded, the pan cools and the fish stews grey.

steps.title: Poach eggs for service
steps.prompt: Put the stages of poaching eggs ahead for a busy brunch in order, from the pan to the plate. One stage does not belong.
steps: Bring water at least 8 cm (3 inches) deep to a bare shiver, with a splash of white vinegar if the chef uses it
Crack each egg, as fresh as you can get, into its own cup and slide it in close to the surface
Poach for about 3 minutes, until the white is set and the yolk still flows
Lift each egg out with a slotted spoon straight into iced water to stop the cooking, then trim any ragged edges
Hold the eggs cold for the time the chef sets
On the order, warm an egg in water at about 70°C (158°F) for about a minute, until warm through
Blot it dry on a cloth and set it on the plate
steps.distractor: Leave the poached eggs in the hot poaching water until the order comes in
steps.why: Fresh eggs, a bare shiver and a cup for each egg keep the whites neat. For service the eggs are poached ahead, stopped in iced water and held cold, then warmed through for about a minute; left waiting in hot water, they keep cooking until the yolks set.

steps.title: Make a French omelette
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a classic French omelette in order, from the bowl to the plate. One stage does not belong.
steps: Beat 3 eggs with a pinch of salt until no streaks of white remain
Heat 15 g (1 tbsp) of butter in a 20 cm (8 inch) egg pan over brisk heat until it foams
Pour in the eggs while the butter foams, before it takes any colour
Stir fast with a fork while shaking the pan, so the eggs set in small, soft curds
Stop stirring after about 30 seconds, while the top is still soft and moist, baveuse
Roll the omelette away from the handle
Turn it out seam down onto the plate, pale, smooth and soft at the centre
steps.distractor: Let the butter brown to a nutty hazelnut colour before the eggs go in
steps.why: The whole omelette takes under a minute, so the eggs are beaten smooth before the butter goes on. They go in as the butter foams, are stirred to small curds and rolled while still moist; browned butter would colour and toughen a French omelette, which leaves the pan pale and soft.

steps.title: Blanch and refresh green vegetables
steps.prompt: Put the stages of blanching and refreshing green beans for service in order. One stage does not belong.
steps: Bring plenty of water, about 10 g of salt to 1 litre (about 1 quart), to a rolling boil, with a bowl of iced water beside it
Drop in the beans a handful at a time, so the water comes straight back to the boil
Boil them uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender
Lift them straight into the iced water to stop the cooking and set the colour
Leave them only until cold, then drain them well
Dry them on a cloth, so no clinging water thins the butter later
At service, finish them in moments in hot butter or sauce
steps.distractor: Put the lid on and add a squeeze of lemon to keep the beans bright
steps.why: The iced water waits before the beans go in, because the refresh must follow at once. A big, salted, uncovered rolling boil cooks them fast and keeps the green; a lid and early acid turn them olive. Drained and dried, they finish in moments at service.

steps.title: Braise short rib in red wine
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a short rib braised in red wine in order, from the sear to the sauce. One stage does not belong.
steps: Season and dry the short rib, then sear it in a little oil in a heavy pot until deep brown on every side
Lift the meat out, pour off most of the fat and soften onion, carrot, celery and garlic
Pour in the red wine, scrape up the fond and reduce it by about half
Add the stock and return the meat, the liquid a third to halfway up its sides
Add a bouquet garni, bring it just to a simmer and cover the pot
Braise in a low oven, about 150 to 160°C (302 to 320°F), until a fork slides in and out with no pull
Lift out the meat, strain the liquid and skim off the fat
Reduce the liquid until it coats a spoon, season it and warm the meat through in it
steps.distractor: Boil it hard on the stove so the collagen softens faster
steps.why: The sear and its fond come first, because they flavour the sauce, and the wine is reduced before the stock so it loses its raw edge. Liquid partway up, a lid and a low oven melt the collagen slowly; a hard boil leaves the meat dry and stringy.

steps.title: Build and bake a fish en papillote
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a fish fillet baked en papillote, in a parchment heart, in order. One stage does not belong.
steps: Cut a heart of parchment about 30 to 35 cm (12 to 14 inches) across and brush it with butter
Lay a bed of fine julienne of leek, carrot and fennel on one half, with sliced shallot and herbs
Set the seasoned fillet on the bed with a knob of butter and 15 to 30 ml (1 to 2 tbsp) of white wine
Fold the paper over and crimp the edges in small, tight, overlapping folds all the way round
Twist the tip so no steam can escape
Bake on a tray at about 200°C (392°F), roughly 12 to 15 minutes for a fillet 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick
Probe a test parcel through the paper for 63°C (145°F) at the thickest point
Send it at once, while the parcel is still puffed
steps.distractor: Leave the edges loosely folded so the steam can escape as it bakes
steps.why: The aromatics are cut fine and laid first, so the fish sits on them and they cook in its time. Tight crimps and a twisted tip trap the steam that cooks the fish; loose folds let it out, so the fish dries and the parcel never puffs.

steps.title: Deglaze and finish a pan sauce
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a pan sauce made in the searing pan in order, while the meat rests. One stage does not belong.
steps: Sear the meat in a stainless or carbon steel pan, then lift it out to rest
Pour off all but about 15 ml (1 tbsp) of the fat and lower the heat
Sweat a finely chopped shallot for a minute, soft and without colour
Pour in the wine and scrape up the fond with a flat wooden spatula
Reduce the wine almost dry, au sec
Add the stock, reduce it to nappe and tip in the meat's resting juices
Off the heat, swirl in cold butter a piece at a time until the sauce is glossy
Season it and serve it at once
steps.distractor: Bring the sauce back to a hard boil after the butter goes in, to thicken it
steps.why: The fat is poured off and the shallot sweated before the wine lifts the fond. The wine goes almost dry before the stock so its raw taste cooks away, and the butter goes in last, off the heat: boiled after mounting, the sauce breaks and turns greasy.

steps.title: Bread and fry at the station
steps.prompt: Put the stages of breading and deep frying a piece of seafood in order, from the board to the pass. One stage does not belong.
steps: Pat the seafood dry and season it
Dredge it in flour and shake off the excess, keeping one hand for the dry
Dip it in the egg wash with the other hand, the wet hand
Press it into the crumbs until it is coated all over
Rest the breaded pieces a few minutes so the coating sets
With the oil at about 175°C (347°F), lower the basket gently, no more than half full
Fry until golden, then lift the basket and shake it over the oil
Turn the food onto a rack, salt it at once and send it straight away
steps.distractor: Fill the basket to the top so the whole order fries in one load
steps.why: Flour dries the surface so the egg clings, and the egg glues on the crumbs; a short rest sets the coat. A half-full basket keeps the oil hot so the crust sets fast; an overloaded one drops the heat and the food soaks up fat. Salt it on the rack while hot.

steps.title: Flambé a pan sauce
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a flambé pan sauce of brandy and green peppercorn in order, made at the stove. One stage does not belong.
steps: Sear the steaks, lift them out to rest and pour off most of the fat
Sweat shallot with drained green peppercorns
Pull the pan off the flame and pour in about 60 ml (1/4 cup) of brandy from a measuring jug
Return the pan and tilt its far edge to the flame to light it, a lid within reach
Stand back and let the flame burn out on its own
Add brown stock and reduce it by half
Add cream and simmer it to nappe
Off the heat, swirl in cold butter and serve
steps.distractor: Pour more brandy from the bottle into the pan while it is still alight
steps.why: The spirit goes in off the flame from a measure, never the bottle, because fire can travel back up the neck. It is lit with a lid in reach and left to burn out before the stock, and the sauce is reduced after, so no harsh, boozy edge remains.

match.title: Methods and their heat
match.prompt: Match each cooking method to the heat and the medium that cook the food.
pairs: A thin film of hot fat in a wide pan, the food tossed or turned

Submerged in oil at about 170 to 190°C (338 to 374°F)
